prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, and for the experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B048 as a single-part prize, now with a narrower and more explicit citation as the chair asked. The Kane-Mele idea is that spin-orbit coupling alone, with time-reversal symmetry unbroken, produces a Z2-classified insulator with protected helical edge states. That is a new symmetry class of electronic matter, not a refinement of the integer quantum Hall story. It was tested within a year in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group, where edge-channel conductance was measured, and it was then followed by ARPES maps of surface states in Bi-based materials, which is the kind of link between calculated and measured band structure that I trust. More than fifteen years of replication, a stable interpretation, and a lasting change in how materials are searched and classified give it the maturity I require. Round 1 did not change my reading of the physics. It showed that every colleague who commented accepts the experimental maturity of B048, and the disputes are about credit and about overlap with 2016, not about whether the discovery is real.
statement.case_against: The credit remains the weak point. Three names leave out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, whose HgTe proposal made the Molenkamp experiment targeted, and the three-dimensional topological insulator contributors (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan). Zhang's death does not remove the problem, it only shows that any three-person cut excludes someone. The citation is compound, joining a prediction and an experiment, and I cannot confirm from memory how well HgTe edge conductance quantisation has been reproduced outside the Molenkamp group; the measured conductance is imperfect for longer channels. I also have to admit that B049 has the broadest support (six of eight members), a cleaner two-name credit, and no comparable attribution gap. My remaining disagreement with it is about weight, not about maturity: it is a measurement capability in a field honoured in 2005 and 2012, whereas B048 is a new state of matter. I accept that this is a judgment on which reasonable members differ.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B048 as his best alternative to B024 and asks that the citation reward the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, not topological matter in general. He also notes that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation and that the 3D work blurs the boundary.
responses.response: I agree and have changed the citation to say so: it is confined to the time-reversal-invariant quantum spin Hall state and the HgTe quantum well experiment, with no wording about topological phases in general. That also answers the 2016 overlap question, since the prize would name a different symmetry class and a different observable. On Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, I think the committee's background text should credit the HgTe proposal explicitly, and I accept that a three-name limit forces a hard choice that some will find unsatisfying. On B024 I still defer to you on reactor physics. I take your point that it is clean and mature, but I weigh a new class of matter above a parameter of an established framework, and the 2015 prize makes B024 look more like a continuation than B048 does.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from B045 to B049 and keeps B048 as his first alternative. He finds the physics persuasive but says the credit is not clean because Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D work are hard to separate, and he asks whether overlap with the 2016 prize is fatal.
responses.response: I do not think the 2016 overlap is fatal and I will give the argument. The 2016 prize covered topological defects and the integer quantum Hall topology in a strong magnetic field, with broken time-reversal symmetry. Kane and Mele's state needs no magnetic field, is protected by time-reversal symmetry, and its signature is a pair of counter-propagating helical edge channels. On credit I concede that you are right that the committee fixes one of several plausible sets. My argument is that Kane and Mele have the original idea, and Molenkamp has the first measurement. I also noticed that you moved to B049 because the inventor there is unambiguous. That is a fair point and it is the best argument against my own configuration, though I still count the weaker novelty of B049 against it.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B049 first on measured, reproduced performance of about 1e-18 and a clean two-name credit, and in round 1 raised the prior lineage of the 2005 comb prize and the ion-control prize of 2012 as the main overlap risk.
responses.response: I accept that the reproducibility of B049 is excellent and that its credit is cleaner than B048. Your own text lists the same overlap and the same issue that Ye's role is performance leadership as much as invention. The chair asks whether the geodesy and constants tests have delivered discovery content, and as I read the round-1 statements they have not yet, since they are prospective. If the committee judges that a prize for a clock is a prize for a new tool, I would not call it wrong. I would call it a different kind of prize from the one I prefer. If the committee prefers it to B048, I can support B049 as my fallback with Katori and Ye as the named pair, and I would ask that the citation stay on the magic-wavelength concept.

responses.point: Olsson applies the test of an original idea realised in an actual instrument and verified by independent laboratories, and asks whether Ye's contribution is second-wave execution relative to Katori's proposal and first realisation.
responses.response: By your own test B048 also passes: Kane and Mele supply the original idea, Molenkamp the first realisation, and many groups have verified it. The difference is that B048 has a theory-plus-experiment attribution gap, whereas for B049 you worry that Ye is an excellent second wave. Neither problem is decisive and neither removes the science. If the committee decides on B049, I would support your question, and I would not drop Ye, because the many-body and 1e-18 work is part of what made the idea a clock and not only a proposal.

responses.point: Pearce proposes a two-part prize with B049 and B047 and defers to Eriksson and Mehlig on condensed-matter physics. He says B048 needs the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang credit question resolved.
responses.response: Thank you for deferring on the physics, and I defer to you on IceCube. The cap of three unique people means that the pairing of B049 with B048 is impossible as well, since five names do not fit. So I would ask the committee to treat the choice as a single-part decision. On credit for B048, I cannot resolve it by argument. I can say that the citation now credits what the three people did and makes no claim to cover all of topological matter. I agree that B047 would be hard to defend with Halzen as the sole name, and I would not support it as a second part.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a compound theory-plus-experiment citation that omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D topological insulator contributors.
Whether colleagues outside condensed matter will treat the 2016 topological prize as covering this discovery; I think it does not, but I cannot settle that for them.
How firmly the quantisation of edge conductance in HgTe has been reproduced beyond the Molenkamp group; I am relying on memory and not on a check of the primary papers.
Whether the committee reads B049 as a discovery-class result. If it does, I would see its broader support and cleaner credit as a strong reason to prefer it, and I regard it as a legitimate fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with the credited names of B048, B049 or B016. My Uppsala electronic-structure and magnetism work is adjacent to topological and moire materials, but I have no collaboration with Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. I chaired the 2025 cycle and was a committee expert in 2023 and 2024, which matters only for questions of overlap with recent prizes. Nothing has changed since round 1.
